correctness.rationale: The frozen statement for every t>0 is false under Definition 2.1. For a counterexample take n=2, a=4, r=|z|, and ψ the angle of (|z₁|,|z₂|) in the positive quadrant. Start with B(2) union the open horn {r>1, |ψ−π/4|<c r^(−8)} for small c>0, and delete the compact torus {r=1, ψ=π/4}. The remaining domain is connected: in the ball, vary the modulus direction off π/4 at fixed r≠1 and then move radially to zero; at r=1 the direction already avoids the torus. The outer part attaches to the remaining ball at 1<r<2. It is Reinhardt and contains B(1/2); for r≥2 the unchanged connected angular slices have measure 2c r^(−8), stay uniformly inside the positive quadrant, and intersect only at X*=(1,1)/√2. Yet the rays omit t=1. The cited Eq. (5.2) in [1] asserts full-line inclusion without an intermediate-radius hypothesis, and does not remedy this counterexample. The delivered repair restricts the result to t>R. Re-audit: (2.3) ensures every required phase point and fixed-radius phase path there. The finite monomial map is an immersion by its constant and linear coordinates. Its projective speed is a variance: the weight A_(m−1)/A_m times t^(−2) controls the degree variance because the lower layers and the squared mean deficit contribute O(t^(−4)). This yields the uniform radial tail, and diagonal rotations cost O(t^(−1)). All other phase classes are separated in the projective limit by ratios of degree-m entries differing by one coordinate exponent, and the vanishing constant entry excludes limits in the original domain. Uniform convergence and compactness give the embedding; the same exponent differences give exactly the diagonal kernel of the limiting covariance. The degree-one normalization independently gives squared speed A₀A₁/(A₀+A₁t²)². No argument uses the deleted range of radii or equates the limiting angular tensor with an intrinsic boundary metric. Complete affected files are repairs/1/RESULT.md and repairs/1/VERIFICATION.md.

value.rationale: Identifying an actual torus in a metric completion is more informative than incompleteness or a projective closure alone. The result distinguishes noncollapsing relative phases from common rotations and gives a coefficient measuring the cost of escape in the natural Bergman length. The repair removes only the extraneous small-radius assertion and retains these structural conclusions in all allowed polynomial degrees, while distinguishing the limiting tensor from any boundary length metric.
